ian: quick report from onboarding run for argo-90k (int4v2-exp). reproducible sync point: ~47.2k tokens we see a single-token desync and kvcache read returning next-block. small latency blip too.
harsha: can you paste repro command and a short log snippet?
ian: repro: ./ci/onboard_long.sh --model argo-90k --quant int4v2x --seq 92000 --batch 1 --seed 3 --mode long-fuzz
log: 
```
[kv] shard=0 read_pos=47204 expected_block=369 got_block=370
[rot] accum=47204.998 -> recompute=47205.000 delta=0.002
[token] out: "there" -> then "\n" at pos 47211
[perf] token_latency: 170ms -> 208ms
```
sylvie: interesting delta in recompute. fp16 path?
ian: fp16 clean to 92k. int4v2x and int3 show issue. int8 fine.
harsha: suggests accumulation rounding in quant rotary or LUT interpolation. did you try the renorm guard?
ian: ran with ROTARY_GUARD=on (cheap 16-lane check every 1k tokens): guard flagged at 47k and forced renorm; after that drift still occurred later at ~61k.
ops-bot: snapshot saved s3://redwood-ci/argo/1844449999/snap.tgz (tags: int4v2x,rotary-guard)
sylvie: could eviction timing amplify small rounding differences into a persistent write misalignment. try KV_EVICT_SYNC=1 and KV_PREFETCH=0 to remove async variance.
ian: ran sync-evict + pref off: drift moved to ~58k but still reproducible.
harsha: next steps: 1) bisect quant kernel impl scalar vs vector (harsha) 2) add cheap phase checksum in kernel every 512 tokens (ian) 3) try mixed-precision rotary compute (sylvie)
sylvie: I'll prototype fp32 phase accumulation for int4 path (compute sin/cos in fp32 for phase, keep rest quantized). should be low-cost and may remove rounding accumulation.
ian: added lightweight checksum to kernel behind flag DEBUG_PHASE=1 and reran; checksum diverges exactly at the read_pos mismatch. looks like phase->index rounding flips by 1 at that moment.
harsha: if mixed-precision removes repro, cool. otherwise we should add a safe fallback: on sequences>32k use conservative rotary path or enforce periodic full recompute.
sylvie: mixed-precision trial: initial runs show no divergence up to 100k (3 trials). perf hit ~6% on throughput. can we gate it behind long-seq heuristic?
ian: agreed. will wire runtime config: ROTARY_SAFE_FOR_LONGSEQ=true which switches to mixed-precision if seq_len>32k. also add telemetry event when safe path used.
bench-bot: scheduled matrix job 1844449999-matrix with quant=[int3,int4v2x,int4v2] x evict=[async,sync] x renorm=[off,guard] x safepath=[on,off]. results to s3://redwood-ci/argo/matrix/1844449999/
harsha: plan: if mixed-precision consistently prevents drift, ship safepath as hotfix and follow up with kernel rewrite for perf. assign owners: harsha (kernel bisect + perf rewrite), sylvie (mixed-precision impl + PR), ian (matrix runs + telemetry).
ian: thanks all. will post bench results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
